interfaces.name: PoseSourceProvider
interfaces.pre: start() only after selectPoseSource returned ok. onFrame/onError are the only consumers.
interfaces.post: Every frame passed to onFrame satisfies the PoseFrame contract, is sanitized (SEC-1), has strictly increasing timestampMs and frameIndex counting from 0 per start() (REC-3). After stop() returns no callback fires. start() while running stops the previous session first (CON-1).
interfaces.errors: Never throws. permission_denied / camera_error -> onError once, provider stops (FAIL-5). No delivered frame for POSE_STALL_MS while running -> onError('stalled') once per stall (REC-1).

interfaces.name: RawPoseResult + toPoseFrame
interfaces.pre: raw comes only from mediapipeBinding / MediapipePoseView (the binding converts the library's native shape into RawPoseResult).
interfaces.post: Returns sanitizePoseFrame(frame): landmarks 1-10 = {x:0,y:0,z:0,visibility:0}; x,y and visibility clamped to [0,1]; missing visibility -> 0 (fail closed).
interfaces.errors: Returns null (caller increments stats.dropped) when landmarks.length !== 33, any x/y/z/timestamp is non-finite, or imageWidth/imageHeight <= 0 (FAIL-3).

interfaces.name: SKELETON_BONES + projectSkeleton
interfaces.pre: view = Canvas layout size in px; camera preview uses cover fit.
interfaces.post: Cover fit: s = max(vw/iw, vh/ih), ox = (vw - iw*s)/2, oy = (vh - ih*s)/2, px = (mirrored ? 1 - x : x)*iw*s + ox, py = y*ih*s + oy. Joints with visibility < minVisibility (default 0.5) omitted; a bone is drawn only if both ends are drawn. Indices 0-10 never appear (SEC-2).
interfaces.errors: view width/height <= 0 -> empty skeleton.

Colors colors.skeletonJoint / colors.skeletonBone, radius sizes.jointDot/2, stroke from an existing borders.* token - tokens only (lint:tokens).

interfaces.errors: Unknown keys dropped; badges must be unique catalog ids (<= 7); wearables <= 7; archetype.name must match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z .'-]{0,39}$; numbers finite and in plausible ranges; complete() kinds refused/rate_limited/llm_error and empty text -> full refund before responding.

interfaces.name: HTTP voice-debrief (v2) and voice-qa
interfaces.signature:
POST /functions/v1/voice-debrief  body: DebriefRequest  -> DebriefResponse (statuses above)
POST /functions/v1/voice-qa       body: { seconds: integer 0..120 } (0 = read remaining) -> 200 { ok: true, grantedSeconds, remainingSeconds } | 400 | 401 | 413
interfaces.pre: Authorization: Bearer <user JWT>. Secrets only from Deno.env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_VOICE_*, ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID?, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, QA_CAP_SECONDS? (default 300).
interfaces.post: Deployed by Person B in D2.3. Tier 3 conversation itself is out of scope; voice-qa is the single enforcement point it must call.
interfaces.errors: Any body containing a 'system' or 'user' key -> 400 legacy_prompt_rejected (SEC-5).

interfaces.name: Quota RPCs (supabase/migrations/003_voice_usage_rpc.sql - FROZEN AREA, D2.0 only)
interfaces.signature:
create function public.reserve_debrief_chars(p_user_id uuid, p_chars integer, p_cap integer default 16000) returns date   -- reserved month, or null when the cap would be exceeded
create function public.refund_debrief_chars(p_user_id uuid, p_month date, p_chars integer) returns void
create function public.consume_qa_seconds(p_user_id uuid, p_seconds integer, p_cap_seconds integer default 300) returns table (granted integer, remaining integer)
-- all: language plpgsql security definer set search_path = ''
-- revoke execute on function ... from public, anon, authenticated; grant execute ... to service_role;
interfaces.pre: Month = date_trunc('month', timezone('utc', now()))::date computed in SQL. p_chars must be 1..400, p_seconds clamped to 0..120, p_cap clamped to <= 16000, p_cap_seconds clamped to [300, 600] (matches the 001 CHECK).
interfaces.post: reserve: insert (user, month) on conflict do nothing; single UPDATE ... set debrief_chars_used = debrief_chars_used + p_chars WHERE debrief_chars_used + p_chars <= cap RETURNING month. refund: debrief_chars_used = greatest(0, used - p_chars) on the reserved month. consume: insert on conflict do nothing; select qa_seconds_used for update; granted = least(p_seconds, greatest(0, cap - used)); update; remaining = cap - used - granted. No new table, so the RLS compliance check is unchanged.
interfaces.errors: p_chars outside 1..400 -> raise exception; the edge function never sends such values.

interfaces.name: summarizeDebriefUsage + debrief-cost-report CLI (D4.1a)
interfaces.pre: The log file is any text export of the voice-debrief function logs (Person B, D4.1). The script reads that one local file, maps lines through parseUsageLogLine and passes the records to summarizeDebriefUsage.
interfaces.post: No price constant is duplicated: every USD figure comes from costModel.ts exports (ECON-7). The script prints renderCostReport plus the count of skipped lines; it never echoes a raw input line, makes no network call and reads no environment variable (SEC-11).

interfaces.name: Group leaderboard convergence (D4.2a; behaviour only, PitchIqRepository signature unchanged)
interfaces.pre: Builds on REC-4 (D2.3a): every SUBSCRIBED status triggers a refetch. join = subscribeToGroup + SUBSCRIBED; leave = the returned unsubscribe, or CHANNEL_ERROR / TIMED_OUT / CLOSED; rejoin = a later SUBSCRIBED on the same channel or a fresh subscribeToGroup.
interfaces.post: Each trigger (change event or SUBSCRIBED) starts fetch number n = ++started; a resolved fetch is delivered only if it is not closed and n > lastDelivered, then lastDelivered = n (CON-5). The event payload is never read (SEC-12). State-based refetch makes duplicates and reordering harmless (CON-6). Two clients that have each processed their last trigger hold deep-equal snapshots equal to server truth (REC-5). DemoRepository is unchanged.
interfaces.errors: A rejected fetch is swallowed, delivers nothing and leaves lastDelivered unchanged; the next trigger recovers (FAIL-11). After unsubscribe nothing is delivered, even from fetches already in flight, and removeChannel is called exactly once (REC-6).

interfaces.name: ClipEncoder + buildClipEncodeRequest (D6.1a; library-agnostic)
interfaces.pre: width, height, fps and maxDurationMs are derived from INSTAGRAM_EXPORT_SPEC (maxDurationSec * 1000), never retyped.
interfaces.post: buildClipEncodeRequest: startMs = max(0, window.startMs); durationMs = min(maxDurationMs, max(0, window.endMs - window.startMs)) - the same clamp as buildHighlightClipArgs, so startMs/1000 and durationMs/1000 formatted with 3 decimals equal its -ss and -t values (MEDIA-1). isValidClipRequest is true only when both URIs start with file://, differ, startMs and durationMs are finite, startMs >= 0 and 0 < durationMs <= maxDurationMs.
interfaces.errors: Pure; never throws. Any ClipEncoder implementation resolves (never rejects) with a ClipEncodeFailure (FAIL-13).

interfaces.name: highlightEncoderBinding (D6.1a; the only reference to modules/highlight-encoder)
interfaces.pre: NativeHighlightEncoder is the JS contract the Swift/Kotlin module must meet in D6.1 (device work, out of scope here). In Jest the module is provided only by jest.mock('../../../../modules/highlight-encoder', factory, { virtual: true }) inside the test files; jest.setup.js is not edited.
interfaces.post: encode: !isValidClipRequest -> invalid_request without calling native; module unavailable -> unavailable; native resolves and echoes h264 / aac / yuv420p / fastStart true with durationMs <= request.durationMs + CLIP_DURATION_SLACK_MS and a file:// outputUri -> ok; any other echo -> spec_mismatch; native rejects or throws -> encode_failed.
interfaces.errors: isHighlightEncoderAvailable() returns false and never throws when the module is missing, its require throws, or encodeHighlightClip is not a function - Expo Go, Jest, web (FAIL-12).

interfaces.name: HighlightClipService + ClipFiles (D6.1a)
interfaces.pre: recordingUri is the file:// URI returned by expo-camera recordAsync({ maxDuration: 15 }) once the camera-mode machine is in 'record' (device wiring, D6.1). files.cacheDir() returns a file:// directory URI ending in '/'.
interfaces.post: makeClip: recordingUri not file:// or totalDurationMs not finite / <= 0 -> invalid_input (nothing called). Otherwise window = selectPeakStreakWindow(eventTimestampsMs, totalDurationMs); outputUri = `${files.cacheDir()}highlight-${now()}.mp4`; encoder.encode(buildClipEncodeRequest(...)). On success and on failure the raw recording is removed; on failure the partial output is removed if it exists (SEC-14, FAIL-13). No network, no upload.
interfaces.errors: Never rejects: files.exists/remove rejections are swallowed. A makeClip call while another is in flight resolves { ok: false, reason: 'busy' } and touches no file (CON-11).

interfaces.name: CameraModeController (D6.1a; D-5 / D-7 single camera session)
interfaces.pre: Initial state { mode: 'idle', mounted: 'none', switching: false }. UI rule for the D6.1 device wiring: mount MediapipePoseView only while mounted === 'pose' and expo-camera CameraView only while mounted === 'record'.
interfaces.post: request(m) when settled on m resolves ok at once. From mounted 'none' the target mounts immediately. From mounted X to any other target: emit { mounted: 'none', switching: true }, wait for notifyUnmounted(X), then teardownMs on the clock, then emit the target (mounted = m, or 'none' for idle) with switching false (CON-9). A request made while switching replaces the target; the replaced promise resolves superseded and the teardown wait is not restarted or skipped (CON-10).
interfaces.errors: Never rejects or throws. No notifyUnmounted(X) within teardownTimeoutMs -> the pending request resolves teardown_timeout and the controller settles at { mode: 'idle', mounted: 'none', switching: false }; later requests work (REC-7). notifyUnmounted for a kind that is not being torn down is ignored.

interfaces.name: SocialHandoff + socialHandoffBinding (D6.2a)

Success -> { ok: true, via: 'native' }. The Stories payload has backgroundVideo only when videoUri is non-null and attributionURL only for a non-empty https:// URL (SEC-16).

A second share() while one is in flight -> busy with zero dependency calls (CON-12). getNativeSocialHandoff() returns null and never throws when the module is missing, throws, or lacks either method (FAIL-16).

security: SEC-1 Every PoseFrame that leaves src/services/cv has landmarks 1-10 equal to {x:0,y:0,z:0,visibility:0}; mock frames pass through sanitizePoseFrame too.
SEC-2 projectSkeleton and SkeletonOverlay never output joint indices 0-10 or bones touching them, even for an unsanitized input frame.

SEC-3 expo-mediapipe-pose is referenced only by src/services/cv/mediapipeBinding.ts and src/services/cv/MediapipePoseView.tsx; pose landmarker only (no face/hand/segmentation); no camera pixels or PoseFrames are persisted or sent over the network in Day 2-3; check:compliance stays fully green.
SEC-4 The live (mediapipe) source starts only with camera_skeletal_tracking consent and, for minors needing it, parental_verified; simulate still requires camera consent (Day-1 behaviour).

SEC-5 voice-debrief accepts only DebriefRequest v2; a body with a 'system' or 'user' key gets 400 legacy_prompt_rejected; unknown keys are dropped; the prompt is built only server-side from whitelisted numeric/enum fields plus an archetype name matching ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z .'-]{0,39}$.

SEC-6 Strava never reaches a prompt: buildDebriefRequest throws via assertAiSafeSources, and the server rejects any wearables[].source outside {healthkit, health_connect, whoop} with 400 invalid_source before any reserve or LLM call.
SEC-7 RPC user ids come only from the verified JWT, never the body; RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER with search_path '' and EXECUTE granted to service_role only; voice_usage stays client read-only.
SEC-8 No new EXPO_PUBLIC_* variables; ElevenLabs keys are read only by scripts/generate-cue-audio.ts (local shell) and edge functions; the script never prints a key value.
ECON-1 During a drill only bundled Tier 1 cue clips play: CuePlayer accepts module ids only, and nothing in the drill path calls TTS, an LLM, or a streaming voice endpoint.
ECON-2 Debrief text is at most 400 chars (server truncates, client truncates again).

ECON-3 Monthly debrief TTS budget 16 000 chars per user: 400 chars are reserved atomically BEFORE any LLM/TTS call; a refused reservation returns 200 {ok:false, reason:'monthly_cap'} with zero spend; afterwards 400 - text.length is refunded; LLM refusal/error/empty refunds all 400.
ECON-4 Request body <= 8192 bytes (413), server prompt <= 6000 chars, badges <= 7 unique ids, wearables <= 7 records.

ECON-5 Tier 3 Q&A: consume_qa_seconds grants min(requested, cap - used) with cap clamped to [300, 600] s/month (default 300); voice-qa accepts 0..120 s per call; client QaBudget stays clamped to [5, 10] min.
ECON-6 No automatic retries of paid calls: one invoke per debrief(); any failure falls back to the template.

SEC-9 (D4.1a) Telemetry never leaks to the client: every handleDebrief body has exactly the keys {ok, text, audioUrl, usage} with usage exactly {inputTokens, outputTokens} (finite integers >= 0), or exactly {ok, reason}. No body contains any part of the server prompt, the reserved month, a char-budget figure, a user id, an upstream error message or status, or an environment value.

SEC-12 (D4.2a) Realtime payloads are triggers, never data: the postgres_changes handler ignores its argument and refetches through RLS, so a forged or foreign-group event cannot add, remove or alter a leaderboard row.

SEC-13 (D6.1a) modules/highlight-encoder is referenced only by src/services/highlight/highlightEncoderBinding.ts and expo-file-system only by src/services/highlight/clipFiles.ts. clipEncoder.ts, highlightClip.ts and cameraMode.ts import no native, camera, pose, file-system or encoder package (ClipEncoder is library-agnostic). package.json has no dependency matching ffmpeg, vision-camera or nitro (D-4, D-7).

failure: FAIL-1 isMediapipeAvailable() returns false and never throws in Expo Go, Jest and web; the library is required lazily inside try/catch.
FAIL-2 selectPoseSource never substitutes mock frames for a live drill: simulate=false with no native module -> {ok:false, reason:'native_unavailable'} and the existing Dev Client notice.
FAIL-3 toPoseFrame drops (null, stats.dropped++) results with != 33 landmarks, non-finite values or non-positive image size; clamps x, y, visibility to [0,1]; missing visibility -> 0.
FAIL-4 The mediapipe provider drops any result whose timestampMs <= the last delivered timestamp.
FAIL-5 A native permission or camera error calls onError once with permission_denied/camera_error and stops the provider; the runner shows drill-notice; no mock substitution.
FAIL-6 Debrief transport error, timeout (12 s), ok:false or empty text -> template debrief (source 'template', cost 0); zero-key Demo Mode is unchanged.
FAIL-7 voice-debrief TTS failure still returns 200 ok with audioUrl null; the chars stay charged (text.length).
FAIL-8 CuePlayer.play returns false and never throws on a missing source, before prepare(), or on any player exception; the caption still renders.
FAIL-9 prepare() pre-warms each created player once at volume 0 (expo-audio Android first-play silence, #52722).

FAIL-10 (D4.1a) Telemetry can never break a debrief: toUsageRecord, formatUsageLogLine and parseUsageLogLine never throw; a non-200, ok:false, malformed or NaN-usage result yields null (no log line) and the HTTP response is unchanged. summarizeDebriefUsage([]) returns null; the CLI exits 1 on an unreadable file or zero valid records and 2 on a missing argument.

FAIL-11 (D4.2a) A refetch that rejects during convergence is swallowed and delivers nothing; the client keeps its last snapshot, and the next change event or SUBSCRIBED brings it back to server truth.

FAIL-12 (D6.1a) isHighlightEncoderAvailable() returns false and never throws when modules/highlight-encoder is missing, throws on require or lacks encodeHighlightClip; encode() then resolves {ok:false, reason:'unavailable'}.

FAIL-13 (D6.1a) ClipEncoder.encode and HighlightClipService.makeClip never reject: an invalid request never reaches native (invalid_request); a native rejection is encode_failed; an echo that is not h264/aac/yuv420p/fastStart or runs longer than requested + 50 ms is spec_mismatch; on every failure the partial output file is removed.

FAIL-14 (D6.2a) Share always degrades to the OS share sheet: target app not installed, share id missing or malformed, native module absent, TikTok iOS redirect URI or library save unavailable, or a rejecting native call -> openOsShare exactly once. share() never rejects.

FAIL-15 (D6.2a) StickerCapture.capture never rejects: null target -> not_ready without a capture call; a rejecting or throwing captureRef, an empty or non-.png result, or a missing library -> capture_failed.
FAIL-16 (D6.2a) getNativeSocialHandoff() returns null and never throws when modules/social-handoff is missing, throws on require or lacks shareToInstagramReels / shareToTikTok (Expo Go, Jest, web).
reconnection: REC-1 Stall: a running provider with no delivered frame for 1500 ms calls onError('stalled') once per stall; the next valid frame clears it; the engine is not reset.
REC-2 AppState background: the runner stops the provider and calls cuePlayer.stopAll(); an active drill is reset (never resumed) with a drill-notice; on 'active' cuePlayer.reassertAudioMode() runs.
REC-3 start() after stop() begins a new stream: frameIndex restarts at 0 and the previous session's callbacks never fire again.

REC-4 Realtime: subscribeToGroup re-fetches members and calls onChange on every SUBSCRIBED status, including rejoins after CHANNEL_ERROR/TIMED_OUT; unsubscribe removes the channel and silences onChange.

REC-5 (D4.2a) Rejoin convergence: a client that missed any number of changes while its channel was in CHANNEL_ERROR / TIMED_OUT / CLOSED holds, after its next SUBSCRIBED fetch settles, a snapshot deep-equal to server truth and to the snapshot of a client that never disconnected.

REC-6 (D4.2a) Leave / rejoin lifecycle: after unsubscribe no onChange fires for later events or for fetches already in flight, and removeChannel is called exactly once; a fresh subscribeToGroup opens a new channel and delivers current truth on SUBSCRIBED.

REC-7 (D6.1a) Camera teardown that is never acknowledged fails closed: without notifyUnmounted within 1000 ms the request resolves teardown_timeout and the controller settles at idle with nothing mounted; a later request succeeds.
concurrency: CON-1 At most one PoseSourceProvider runs and at most one native camera view is mounted; start() while running stops the previous session first. vision-camera is not installed in Day 2-3 (D-5).
CON-2 One drill consumes frames from exactly one provider kind; changing simulate or drill resets the runner first.
CON-3 reserve/refund/consume RPCs are single transactions under the row lock, so concurrent calls never push debrief_chars_used or qa_seconds_used past the cap.
CON-4 CuePlayer plays one cue at a time; play(id) stops the cue that is playing (latest wins).
CON-5 (D4.2a) Latest-wins refetch: onChange is never called with the result of a fetch that started before a fetch already delivered; a slow early fetch that resolves after a newer one is dropped.

CON-6 (D4.2a) Duplicate and out-of-order change events are harmless: delivering the same event N times, or the same set of events in different orders to two clients, leaves both clients with identical final snapshots equal to server truth.

CON-7 (D4.2a) Canonical order: SupabaseRepository.listGroupMembers returns members in ascending userId order whatever the row order, so the leaderboard ranking (stable sort by bestOvr descending) and computeCrowns tie-breaks are the same on every client.
CON-8 (D4.2a) GroupSessionScreen never replaces a subscription snapshot with the result of its initial listGroupMembers call: the initial result is applied only if no onChange has fired yet.

CON-9 (D6.1a) Single camera session: CameraModeState.mounted is one of none | pose | record, and between any emitted state with mounted X and a later one with mounted Y (X, Y in {pose, record}, X != Y) there is an emitted state with mounted 'none', a notifyUnmounted(X) call and at least teardownMs of clock time. Extends CON-1 to the record camera.

CON-10 (D6.1a) Latest camera request wins: a request made while switching replaces the target, the replaced request resolves superseded, the teardown wait is neither skipped nor restarted, and the final state matches the last request.
CON-11 (D6.1a) One encode at a time: makeClip while another makeClip is in flight resolves busy and removes or writes no file.
CON-12 (D6.2a) One handoff at a time: share() while another share() is in flight resolves busy with zero dependency calls.
